title: Intramedullary Nailing for Femoral Shaft Fractures
official: Comparative Effectiveness Randomized Controlled Trial of Micromotion vs Non-micromotion Intramedullary Nailing for Femoral Shaft Fractures
summary: A randomized controlled trial that is trying to find the best treatment for a severe upper leg (i.e., thigh, also known as femoral shaft) fracture. One type of treatment, which is called micromotion intramedullary (within the hollow center of the bone) nailing, is a type of nail used for thigh fracture treatments that helps to heal the bone by allowing a small amount of controlled movement. Another type, called non-micromotion intramedullary nailing, is also used to treat thigh fractures but does not include this controlled-movement feature. Both treatments are approved by the FDA but have not been directly compared to each other. Participation includes being assigned to receive either a micromotion intramedullary nail or a non-micromotion intramedullary nail. Those that participate will be randomly assigned (like a flip of a coin) to one of those treatment methods and return for standard follow-up visits. In addition to those regular clinical follow-ups, participants will complete some brief surveys/questionnaires while they are in the hospital. Research staff will also look at past medical history.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients aged 18-84 years old inclusive with a femoral shaft fracture deemed appropriate for treatment with an IMN by the treating surgeon

Exclusion Criteria:

* Not within age range
* Planned treatment with dominant implants other than IMN
* Non-ambulatory at baseline
* Fracture needs a planned-staged secondary procedure for bone defects (e.g., Masquelet)
* Any previous surgery on the index site
* Fracture fixation \>28 days from injury
* Fractures that the treating surgeon indicates require any additional fixation that spans the fracture. These patients will be late ineligible
* Patients with a history of infection or a current active infection at the surgical site
* Patients undergoing revision surgery following primary fixation
* Patients undergoing femoral nailing for a pathological fracture
* Patients undergoing bone transport over an intramedullary nail
* Non-English or Non-Spanish speaking
* Prisoners or impending incarceration
* Patients unwilling or unable to participate in study protocol or follow up in the IU system for 12 months
